evidence: Supported by citations to Nicoludis et al., 2015; Rubinstein et al., 2015

claim: K562 cells expressing ΔEC1 or ΔEC4-6 constructs did not aggregate while cells expressing chimeras in which EC1 and EC4 derived from different paralogs did.
source: Analogously, purified EC1-3 constructs failed to dimerize in vitro whereas EC1-4 constructs did (Nicoludis et al., 2015; Rubinstein et al., 2015), and K562 cells expressing ΔEC1 or ΔEC4-6 constructs did not aggregate while cells expressing chimeras in which EC1 and EC4 derived from different paralogs did (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014

claim: The EC1/EC4 interaction is not strictly required for the specificity of dimerization but it drives dimerization affinity through non-specific hydrophobic interactions.
source: Together, these results indicate that the EC1/EC4 interaction is not strictly required for the specificity of dimerization but it drives dimerization affinity through non-specific hydrophobic interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence including the F86A mutant and previous studies

claim: Non-clustered Pcdhs include the δ-1 (Pcdh1, Pcdh7, Pcdh9, Pcdh11) and δ-2 (Pcdh8, Pcdh10, Pcdh17, Pcdh18, Pcdh19) families.
source: These include the δ-1 (Pcdh1, Pcdh7, Pcdh9, Pcdh11) and δ-2 (Pcdh8, Pcdh10, Pcdh17, Pcdh18, Pcdh19) families that are integral to the development and maintenance of the nervous system (Keeler et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about non-clustered protocadherin classification

claim: δ-1 and δ-2 Pcdh families are integral to the development and maintenance of the nervous system.
source: These include the δ-1 (Pcdh1, Pcdh7, Pcdh9, Pcdh11) and δ-2 (Pcdh8, Pcdh10, Pcdh17, Pcdh18, Pcdh19) families that are integral to the development and maintenance of the nervous system (Keeler et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Keeler et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2011

claim: Sequence coevolution analysis successfully predicted the clustered Pcdh interface.
source: We used sequence coevolution analysis, which successfully predicted the clustered Pcdh interface (Nicoludis et al., 2015) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1),to look for evidence of an antiparallel interface in non-clustered Pcdhs (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nicoludis et al., 2015 and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: Most covarying residue pairs in non-clustered Pcdhs were intra-domain structural contacts of the well-conserved cadherin fold.
source: As in clustered Pcdhs, most covarying residue pairs in non-clustered Pcdhs were intra-domain structural contacts of the well-conserved cadherin fold.
evidence: This is an observation from the sequence coevolution analysis

claim: Several covarying pairs in non-clustered Pcdhs are found between EC2 and EC3, or EC1 and EC4, similar to those observed for the clustered Pcdhs.
source: Additionally, several covarying pairs are found between EC2 and EC3, or EC1 and EC4, similar to those observed for the clustered Pcdhs.
evidence: This is an observation from the sequence coevolution analysis

claim: When mapped onto the PcdhγB3 dimer, covarying pairs in non-clustered Pcdhs are somewhat further apart than true interface contacts.
source: When mapped onto the PcdhγB3 dimer, these covarying pairs are somewhat further apart than true interface contacts (Figure 4B), which could be due to differences in dimerization interfaces, as we observe between the clustered Pcdh families, or in the δ-1 or δ-2 Pcdhs secondary structure, for which there are no available structures.
evidence: Supported by mapping shown in Figure 4B

claim: Sequence coevolution analysis predicts an antiparallel EC1-4 interaction in members of the non-clustered Pcdhs.
source: This analysis thus predicts an antiparallel EC1-4 interaction in members of the non-clustered Pcdhs.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the sequence coevolution analysis

claim: Maximum parsimony suggests that the ancestral Pcdh used the antiparallel EC1-4 dimer interaction.
source: However maximum parsimony suggests that the ancestral Pcdh used the antiparallel EC1-4 dimer interaction, and Pcdh members which do not show this interaction mechanism either diverged before it evolved or lost it subsequently.
evidence: This is an inference based on evolutionary reasoning

claim: The predicted EC1/EC4 interface residues in non-clustered Pcdhs are predominantly hydrophobic.
source: The predicted EC1/EC4 interface residues are predominantly hydrophobic, while EC2/EC3 residues have more polar and ionic character (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by amino acid frequency analysis shown in Figure 4C

claim: The predicted EC2/EC3 interface residues in non-clustered Pcdhs have more polar and ionic character.
source: The predicted EC1/EC4 interface residues are predominantly hydrophobic, while EC2/EC3 residues have more polar and ionic character (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by amino acid frequency analysis shown in Figure 4C

claim: Positions 41 and 77 in EC1 and 320, 321, 371 and 373 in EC4 are more hydrophobic in non-clustered than clustered Pcdhs.
source: Notably, positions 41 and 77 in EC1 and 320, 321, 371 and 373 in EC4 are more hydrophobic in non-clustered than clustered Pcdhs, indicating that these may form contacts in some non-clustered Pcdhs.
evidence: This is an observation from the amino acid frequency analysis

claim: In non-clustered Pcdhs, like in the clustered Pcdhs, the EC1/EC4 interaction may promote dimer affinity while the EC2/EC3 interaction provides specificity.
source: Thus, like in the clustered Pcdhs, the EC1/EC4 interaction may promote dimer affinity while the EC2/EC3 interaction provides specificity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed similarity in interface composition between clustered and non-clustered Pcdhs

claim: The PcdhγB3 EC1-4 structure confirms the sequence coevolution analysis, demonstrating the robustness of the analysis.
source: Our structure of PcdhγB3 EC1-4 confirms our sequence coevolution analysis, demonstrating the robustness of the analysis and revealing the molecular details of this interaction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the agreement between the structure and the prediction

claim: Unlike the Dscams, where isoforms vary at specific alternatively-spliced regions, the clustered Pcdh subfamilies are structurally diverse.
source: Unlike the Dscams, where isoforms vary at specific alternatively-spliced regions (Li et al., 2016; Meijers et al., 2007; Sawaya et al., 2008; Wojtowicz et al., 2007), the clustered Pcdh subfamilies are structurally diverse, and thus can encode specificity in different ways.
evidence: This is a comparison with Dscams supported by citations to Li et al., 2016; Meijers et al., 2007; Sawaya et al., 2008; Wojtowicz et al., 2007

claim: Clustered Pcdh subfamilies can encode specificity in different ways.
source: Unlike the Dscams, where isoforms vary at specific alternatively-spliced regions (Li et al., 2016; Meijers et al., 2007; Sawaya et al., 2008; Wojtowicz et al., 2007), the clustered Pcdh subfamilies are structurally diverse, and thus can encode specificity in different ways.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed structural diversity

claim: A hydrophobic interaction between EC1 and EC4 contributes to dimerization affinity.
source: We identified a hydrophobic interaction between EC1 and EC4 that contributes to dimerization affinity, whereas its conservation among clustered Pcdh isoforms suggests that this interaction is not a driver of specificity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural analysis and mutagenesis experiments

claim: The conservation of the EC1/EC4 hydrophobic interaction among clustered Pcdh isoforms suggests that this interaction is not a driver of specificity.
source: We identified a hydrophobic interaction between EC1 and EC4 that contributes to dimerization affinity, whereas its conservation among clustered Pcdh isoforms suggests that this interaction is not a driver of specificity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the conservation pattern

claim: Conserved hydrophobic EC1/EC4 interactions play a general role in affinity.
source: Overall, our data support a general role for conserved hydrophobic EC1/EC4 interactions in affinity, and for highly diversified polar EC2/EC3 contacts in specificity, and sequence analyses suggest that this is conserved in at least some non-clustered Pcdhs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence including structural analysis, ICR values, computational alanine scanning, and mutagenesis

claim: Highly diversified polar EC2/EC3 contacts play a general role in specificity.
source: Overall, our data support a general role for conserved hydrophobic EC1/EC4 interactions in affinity, and for highly diversified polar EC2/EC3 contacts in specificity, and sequence analyses suggest that this is conserved in at least some non-clustered Pcdhs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence including structural analysis, ICR values, and computational alanine scanning

claim: The functional distinction between EC1/EC4 (affinity) and EC2/EC3 (specificity) is conserved in at least some non-clustered Pcdhs.
source: Overall, our data support a general role for conserved hydrophobic EC1/EC4 interactions in affinity, and for highly diversified polar EC2/EC3 contacts in specificity, and sequence analyses suggest that this is conserved in at least some non-clustered Pcdhs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the sequence coevolution analysis of non-clustered Pcdhs

claim: Human PcdhγB3 EC1-4 (residues 1–414, not counting the signal peptide) was cloned into pET21 with a C-terminal hexahistidine tag.
source: Human PcdhγB3 EC1-4 (residues 1–414, not counting the signal peptide) was cloned into pET21 with a C-terminal hexahistidine tag, expressed in BL21 Gold (DE3) Escherichia coli cells in terrific broth.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods

claim: PcdhγB3 EC1-4 was expressed in BL21 Gold (DE3) Escherichia coli cells in terrific broth.
source: Human PcdhγB3 EC1-4 (residues 1–414, not counting the signal peptide) was cloned into pET21 with a C-terminal hexahistidine tag, expressed in BL21 Gold (DE3) Escherichia coli cells in terrific broth.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods

claim: Crystals of PcdhγB3 EC1-4 were obtained by vapor diffusion at room temperature in 0.1 M HEPES pH 7, 4% ethylene glycol, and 5% polyethylene glycol monomethyl ether 500.
source: Crystals were obtained by vapor diffusion at room temperature in 0.1 M HEPES pH 7, 4% ethylene glycol, and 5% polyethylene glycol monomethyl ether 500 in a 0.3 μL protein (12 mg/mL) to 0.3 μL reservoir drop, then cryoprotected with reservoir with 20% glycerol before flash cooling in liquid N2.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods

claim: The PcdhγB3 EC1-4 structure was determined by an iterative molecular replacement search with single domains of the PcdhγA1 EC1-3 structure (PDBID 4zi9) in PHENIX.
source: The PcdhγB3 EC1-4 structure was determined by an iterative molecular replacement search with single domains of the PcdhγA1 EC1-3 structure (PDBID 4zi9) in PHENIX (Adams et al., 2010).
